lines.mean: An elephant has come, one elephant!
Which town is this elephant from?
It is the elephant from Bijapur.
Why did it come here?
It lost its way and arrived.
It brought dried coconut and jaggery.
It shared them with all the children.
Then the elephant ran away.

cues: On every “aane”, Samaya swings one arm like a trunk and takes a heavy elephant step.
Amma asks “Yaavooraane?” and waits. Samaya answers “Bijaapuradaane!” Then both mime sharing kobri-bella and run off on “oodi hoytu”.

lines.mean: Puppy, puppy, do you want a snack?

lines.text: Tindi beku teertha beku ella beku
lines.mean: I want a snack, I want a drink, I want everything!
Puppy, why do you need a snack?
So I can eat, grow strong, and guard the house.
Puppy, if a thief comes, what will you do?

lines.text: LoL loL bau endu koogi aaduve
lines.mean: I will bark lol-lol bow and chase about!
Wait, clever pup — I will go and bring a snack.
There — I will stay and keep watch over your house.

cues: Amma asks each question and waits. Samaya answers as Ziggy, especially a clear “Tindi beku!” and “maneya kaayabeku”.
On “kaLLa bandarenu maaduve?” Samaya barks a big “LoL loL bau!” then sits like a guard dog while Amma pretends to fetch the tindi.

lines.mean: One, two — spread the banana leaf.
Three, four — put down the rice.
Five, six — serve the beLe saaru (dal rasam).
Seven, eight — greens (dantu) for the palya.
Nine, ten — fold up the leaf.
From one to ten, that is how it went.
The meal-game was done.

cues: Sit on the floor and mime each serving: spread a leaf (1–2), drop rice (3–4), pour saaru (5–6), add palya (7–8), then fold the leaf (9–10).
Samaya holds up fingers and says the number on each line. Amma can pause so she can shout “Aidu!” or “Hattu!” by herself.

lines.mean: The bear went to the hill.
The bear went to the hill.
The bear went to the hill.
To have a look around.
What did it see?
What did it see?
The other side of the hill.
The other side of the hill.
That is what the bear saw.
It brought jackfruit.
It mixed in honey.
It fed its cubs.
Then it ate and was happily full.

cues: Stomp like a bear up the hill on the first lines, then peek over a ridge and let Samaya answer “Noditenaadu?” with “Halasu!”
Mime scooping jackfruit, dripping honey, feeding the cubs first, then pat a full tummy on “teegitu”.

lines.mean: Moon uncle, run over here!
Come and play with us, all brightness and charm.
Come and be our playmate.
Run on ahead, come along!
I will bring a sugar-stick.
If any is left, I will give you some too.
If you smile, I will smile.
If you cry, I will cry too.
Wherever I go, you still come along.
Yet you stay far away, over there.
Slowly you grow small (as a slim crescent).
You go behind and in front of us.
Moon uncle, run over here!
Come and play with us, all brightness and charm.

cues: Stand at the window, point to the moon, and pat the floor on each “oodi baa” and “aadu baa” so Samaya can call Chandamama.
Offer a pretend sakkare-kaddi, then tiptoe “mellage sannage” and freeze like a little crescent.

lines.mean: Sister, bring the little pot — I am going for water.
Do bring the little pot.
If the pot breaks, it costs only one kaasu (a tiny coin).
Do bring the little pot.
For water that holds the goodness of the name Govinda.
Do bring the little pot.
For a drink of that nectar, in every way.
Do bring the little pot.
I will go to Bindu Madhava's ghat.
Do bring the little pot.
I will do abhisheka for Purandara Vittala.
Do bring the little pot.

cues: On every “Taare bindigeya”, Samaya places a small cup in Amma’s hands and says the refrain herself.
Walk to the ghat, dip the pot, then Samaya pours a pretend abhisheka and can say “ViTThala” or “Govinda”.
